I’d harden a few things in [`test/orders.js`](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js):

- [`averageItemPrice`](file:///C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L17) should handle `items.length === 0`. Right now it divides by zero, which yields `Infinity` or `NaN` depending on the path. Returning `0` or throwing a clear error would make the behavior explicit.
- [`calcTotal`](file:///C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L3) should validate each item shape before multiplying. If an entry is missing `price` or `qty`, or if those fields are non-numeric, the total can become `NaN` silently.
- [`applyDiscount`](file:///C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L10) should reject or normalize invalid totals and codes. As written, unknown codes are ignored, which is fine if intentional, but malformed totals like strings or `NaN` will propagate bad output.
- [`formatOrder`](file:///C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L21) should guard against missing `order`, missing `order.items`, and non-array `items`. Otherwise it will throw before producing any output.
- [`formatOrder`](file:///C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L22) also assumes each item has `name`, `price`, and `qty`. If that data comes from users or external systems, it should either sanitize or fail fast with a clear message.

If you want, I can turn that into a minimal hardening patch that keeps the current API intact.
